Kingdom's Deck is an undemanding strategy game that is perfect for filling in time when you are looking for something to kill about 30 minutes to an hour. Thanks to simple and easy-to-understand mechanics that are common in other games, you can get into the game almost immediately, and it flows nicely without unnecessary delays. Building a kingdom, working with cards, and basic resource management work reliably and can entertain you for a short time without requiring deep concentration. On the other hand, you have to take into account that Kingdom's Deck doesn't bring anything particularly new to the table—the mechanics are rather standard and well-known from other games of the same genre. So if you're looking for original ideas or significant innovations, the game probably won't surprise you. However, it works very well as a quick, relaxing snack for short gaming sessions. If you're not looking for this type of game and you know what genre you're getting into, I would wait for a discount. [b]Price/Fun 6/10 [/b]

100%. Maybe 99%? I picked this game up on sale awhile back and waited to play it for the first time on stream. It's a much smaller game, so I wasn't expecting to grow, it was really just a fun and unique stream for my followers. But here's my thoughts from the four hours streaming: I love it! It reminds me of 9 Kings, which was also fun but I've struggled to get back into it since their recent updates. It has the same basic style of build, fight with superpowers from afar while you watch your soldiers battle, win, then repeat with some quests and selection from cards involved. There's some differences too, the base building is far more in-depth in this game, your control over your soldiers is much greater, and you need to be much more strategic about troop placements. Enemies will often come from up to 4 different directions and you need to defend against every one of them at the same time. So you'll need to take a little time to think about where you're sending your troops, but honestly that's just more of a plus to me. There's some alternate game modes that are like challenge modes, but I can't speak on that yet. I only played the equivalent of "normal" on this stream. The game says I've completed about 17% of the game during my four hour stream, which for $10 means if I maintain that progress, I'll finish the game in about 24 hours. Which honestly feels like great value, and I got it half off so that's all for $5. You will get your value back if you buy this game- no doubt about it. Every level feels very similar.... yet just different enough to keep it interesting. Every one introduces just a few possible cards to make things seem always fresh, and the map alters where enemies come from and what shape your kingdom is. They did a great job with how much variation they introduced with this. I do have one complaint, which is why I said 99%. Which is that I had to start over the tutorial because of a bug that probably only happened because I was streaming. The tutorial at a certain point lets the timer run, but I didn't notice I could pause my first time through. I was reading the cards to my audience when it tried to end the day, but because I didn't place the card it was expecting so it could continue teaching, it got stuck on that screen infinitely producing resources. Like I said, tiny bug. I probably would never have seen it if I wasn't streaming and so trying to keep my audience aware of what we were looking at. So overall, 10/10, or if I want to be maximum pickiness, 9.99/10. The game is great, every game has some random tiny bugs and with that being the only one I saw, I have no reason to actually be upset over it. If you like city builders, strategy, or non-conventional roguelites, pick this game up. You will have a blast.

The modern gaming landscape has warped people into not really understanding what a bad game is. Bare in mind I picked this up in 70% off sale so it cost me the same as a bottle of fizz. It is simple and easy and once you have your strategy that works you can repeat that until you see credits roll. It's shallow but there is some mental engagement required, it looks pretty, it functions as intended with no bugs. A real shame as I feel with a £5 price tag instead of a £8.50 tag than the reviews would be much more positive as it feels more akin to a £5 game. Having said that a lot of people are leaving negative reviews and giving the impression that the game is bad when really it's just a little pricey and bareboned and does not deserve a lot of the negative reviews it's getting. One of the few games I own out of over 1,000 between this, Epic and GOG that i really feel would have benefitted from a 'Meh' review option. This is being voted as bad when really it's fine just bland. This is also a solo developed indie game and should be regarded as such. I've seen much bigger with far more create games that where far less.

这款游戏我不知道到底是算塔防还是召唤，只能说是放置类游戏（史低18.9r入） 里面有箭塔、魔法塔、速射塔、射石炮等好几种攻击塔，再加上堡垒本身和开了攻击的兵营，应该算塔防的一种，但实际上除了安息之地模式，一局10回合下来也就能建个15座塔，不然要么影响生产，要么连回合都过不去，而且塔的强度相当之低；里面还有战士、弩手、刀斧手、皮卡、大弓等好几种小兵，应该算召唤的一种，但实际上兵不仅数量少+复活有代价，还占人口+吃大量粮，如果不是没有近战兵拉不住怪的仇恨，除了弩手我都不想要。 说完了模糊的定位，再来说强行延长游戏时长的成就（每关至少需要3次）。如果每一关第一局打的是普通难度用来熟练地形（不考虑最低难度），那么完成一张地图需要打4次，哪怕第一次就直接完成了最高难度的安息之地模式，也还是要打征服者和暴风雨模式，因为每关的每个难度都有一个成就，这对于成就党来说极不友好！一张地图能二刷就已经算是很好了（一次熟悉+一次高难度），不能用质量不高的地图来拖延玩家的进程。地图数量不多也不是玩家的问题。 最后再来说说游玩中的问题。怪物是海量的，路线是死板的，小兵是少的可怜的，强度是低的可怜的，索敌是会重复浪费的（点名批评超远距但射速极慢的魔法塔），资源是溢出的（1个2级+1个3级资源点就能在第10波溢出300点资源，我都不敢想无尽模式有什么好打的），爽感是几乎没有的，技能是永远差丝血的。 最后说一下可以利用的bug： ①如果金币赌木材/石材失败了，可以直接“ESC-重启天数”重新获得一个赌的机会，两次的结果没有关系（不会固定一个，但也不会上次失败这次成功）。 ②在点击“开始战斗”之前点击“Q”或者“E”，有概率卡出一个免费的技能，释放之后不计入技能CD（相当于开局有个技能能放2次）。
